convertibility_reason: Uses only built-in iBullsPower indicator. Standard MT5 Trade library for order execution. Simple entry/exit rules with fixed pip SL/TP and trailing stop. No external custom indicators or complex money management. Hedging check is platform-specific but logic is straightforward to replicate.

derived_values.name: m_digits_adjust - digit-adjusted point value for SL/TP/trailing calculations
pos1pre - Bulls Power value at bar index 2
pos2cur - Bulls Power value at bar index 1
derived_values.used_by: sell entry condition (declining check and positive check), buy entry condition (negative check)

other_exits: No explicit signal-based close or opposite-side close logic. Positions are only managed via trailing stop; no exit-on-signal-reversal.

position_sizing.conditional_logic: Sell gate allows total<2 positions (up to 2 including both sides). Buy gate allows total<1 (only when no positions exist). Asymmetric position limits.

custom_logic_notes: EA requires hedging account mode (ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_HEDGING) and fails initialization otherwise. Sell entry is a two-condition AND: Bulls Power declining (bar[2] > bar[1]) AND Bulls Power bar[1] still positive (>0). Buy entry is single condition: Bulls Power bar[1] is negative (<0). Position count check is asymmetric: sell allows total<2, buy allows total<1. The Comment() display labels pos1pre as 'BullsPower' and pos2cur as 'BearsPower' but both are actually Bulls Power values at different bar shifts — this is a labeling error in the source code. Trailing stop modifies SL to (current_price - TrailingStop*adjusted_point) for longs and (current_price + TrailingStop*adjusted_point) for shorts, but only moves in TrailingStep increments.
python_conversion_notes: The iBullsPower indicator is equivalent to EMA(close,13) - LOW in the Elder Ray system. In Python, calculate EMA(13) on close prices, then Bulls Power = Low - EMA(13). The digit adjustment logic (multiply by 10 for 3/5-digit brokers) must be replicated: if price has 3 or 5 decimal places, SL/TP/Trailing values in 'pips' need to be multiplied by 10*point. The hedging requirement means the EA can hold both long and short simultaneously — Python implementation needs to track individual positions rather than net position. Trailing stop logic is standard: for long, if Bid - OpenPrice > TrailingStop*adj, and current SL < Bid - (TrailingStop+TrailingStep)*adj, then move SL to Bid - TrailingStop*adj. Mirror for short. Entry signals use completed bars (shift 1 and 2), not current bar, so they should be evaluated once per new bar in Python to avoid repeated signals, even though the original EA lacks a new-bar guard.
